matters.title: Forward looking infrared (FLIR) Skyway Bridge pedestrian and wrong way driver detection system.
matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT)
Title: Forward looking infrared (FLIR) Skyway Bridge pedestrian and wrong way driver detection system.
Agency number: DOT-SSC-22-7021-EG - PUR 7778
Commodity codes: 46161500 Traffic control
Posting: EXTENDED UNTIL 3/29/2022 - 4:30PM ******************************************************************************************************************* FDOT NOTICE OF INTENDED DECISION TO ENTER INTO A SINGLE SOURCE CONTRACT (PUR 7778) This notice of intended decision to enter into a single source contract is posted in accordance with section 287.057(3)(c), Florida Statutes. Failure to file a protest within the time prescribed in Section 120.57(3), F.S., or failure to post the bond or other security required by law within the time allowed for filing a bond shall constitute a waiver of proceedings under Chapter 120, F.S. If the notice advises of the bond requirement and a bond or statutorily authorized alternate is not posted when required, the agency shall summarily dismiss the petition.
Short Description: FLIR system for detecting pedestrians and wrong way drivers on the Sunshine Skyway Bridge. This system includes 10 FLIR cameras, FLIR FLUX software, server and license to get a functional system. It also includes commissioning support to bring the system on- line and working.
Commodity: Traffic control products (commodity code 46161500): Eight FLIR ITS-617 Dual AID 316L (24Vac) Dual-vision sensor for Automatic Incident Detection Two FLIR ITS-644 Dual AID 316L (24Vac) Dual-vision sensor for Automatic Incident Detection Ten wall/pole mount for ITS Dual Ten Sunshield ITS-Series DUAL–316L One FLIR FLUX Software Includes: • One server license • One embedded clustering library license • Ten video pack license One Dell PowerEdge R540 Rack Server Ten warranty - Year four (per sensor) Ten warranty - Year five (per sensor) One software assurance, includes cyber security updates and critical patches/upgrades (annual fee) One commissioning support- Three days onsite
Requestor: Edward Albritton, Florida Department of Transportation, District 7 Traffic Operations.
Requirements: This is a pilot project approved by Derek Volmer in Central Office Testing and Research Lab (TERL) and is not yet on the approved product list. This is new technology that District 7 Traffic Operations wishes to pilot to determine the effectiveness.
Intended Source: Control Technologies Price: $151,828.60 _______________________________________________________________________________________ PUR 7778 (rev. 10/14) Page 1 of 2 60A-1.010, F.A.C. DocuSign Envelope ID: 537303DD-897D-41B2-AB7E-A7A0C84DFF63 STATE OF FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION 375-040-54 FDOT NOTICE OF INTENDED DECISION PROCUREMENT 01/16 TO ENTER INTO A SINGLE SOURCE CONTRACT (PUR 7778)
Justification: The FLIR detection system is a thermal camera-based system capable of detecting wrong-way vehicles, stopped vehicles, and pedestrians. This system combines thermal and visual imaging technology with advanced video analytics to provide a complete solution for automatic incident detection, data collection, and early fire detection. Its traffic video analytics have shown their effectiveness worldwide along highways and in tunnels and are now combined with the power of thermal imaging that allows traffic operators to see clearly in total darkness, in bad weather, and over a long range. It can provide a number of user-friendly advantages, including 24/7 traffic incident detection regardless of weather conditions, real-time visual incident verification and possible forensic evidence after an incident, corrosion-free stainless-steel housing, small form factor allowing for installation anywhere, hassle-free optical zoom block with focus assist, a nano-coated window for optical sensor avoiding the need for a wiper, and a high-end thermal vision core with germanium window. FLIR software and FLIR closed-circuit television (CCTV) are propriatery. Control Technologies is the only authorized reseller of the FLIR products in the state of Florida. Notice of intended single-source purchase, Department of Health (DOH)
Title: Nucleic Extraction Instruments
Agency number: EXP2435
Commodity codes: 41113000 Chemical evaluation instruments and supplies
Posting: The Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Public Health Laboratories needs to purchase nucleic acid extraction instruments to replace the existing Roche MagNA Pure LC 2.0 and MagNA Pure Compact instruments. The instrument must be validated and approved by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for public health emergency preparedness activities, including pandemic influenza and Laboratory Response Network methods for detecting bioterrorism threat agents and emerging infectious diseases. BPHL needs an instrument that will extract up to 24 samples at a time within a short turnaround time to provide results as quickly as possible. The Public Health Laboratory Response Network performance measures state that LRN laboratories must have quick turnaround time for testing samples related to public health. In accordance with Chapter 60A-1.045, Florida Administrative Code, the Department of Health requests authorization to purchase 3 MagNa Pure 24 laboratory instruments, as a single source from Roche Diagnostics Corporation.

BPHL needs an instrument that will extract up to 24 samples at a time within a short turnaround time to provide results as quickly as possible. The Public Health Laboratory Response Network performance measures state that LRN laboratories must have quick turnaround time for testing samples related to public health. The Department of Transportation, State Materials Office, is requesting information from prospective vendors regarding their ability to supply the commodities and/or contractual services attached. KNOWN VENDOR: Kessler Soils Engineering Products, Inc. Vendor information must be received by 5:00PM (EST) on April 7, 2022 at the address listed in this posting. Short Description: MIT Scan
Commodity: 41111615, 41111623
Quantity: One (1) Year
Requestor: State Materials Office, Guangming Wang, State Pavement Performance Engineer ,
Requirements: In support of our mission critical data collection process for monitoring, assessing, and reporting on the condition, performance, and safety of Florida’s roadways, the FDOT’s MIT SCAN is a magnetic imaging tool specifically developed for measuring dowel and tie bar alignments in concrete pavement. Our old MIT SCAN is more than 10 years old and needs a set-up of a rail system for measurements. It is time consuming for set-up and not user-friendly on data transfer and processing. The new MIT SCAN is a totally new device allowing the operator to measure and evaluate pavement joints in real-time without using a rail system. It is very flexible, rapid, efficient, and cost-effective. It will be a great tool for quality assurance and quality control on concrete paving process. In addition, it can be used for forensic investigations of falling joints in existing pavements as well.
Intended Source: Kessler Soils Engineering Products, Inc.
Amount: $71,355.00
Justification: The KSE Testing Equipment (KSE) is the sole distributor for MIT Magnetic Tomography NDT equipment in the USA. As such, KSE is the only vendor that can install, configure, and calibrate the hardware and software required to operate the MIT SCAN.

Posting: The Department of Health’s Division of Disease Control and Health Protection has the need to purchase software maintenance agreements for the existing Geographic Information System (GIS). GIS software and data formats allow the department to quickly share critical information with partners who also utilize Environmental Systems Research Institute (ESRI) storage and communication platforms; providing the infrastructure to both prepare for and respond to environmental health events that have the potential to or directly affect human health. Requirements: Pursuant to s. 943.325 Florida Statute, the FDLE Regional Operations Centers throughout the state operate crime laboratories with the specific mission of investigating high profile criminal case work. To accomplish this, FDLE must utilize specific implements and software in the Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) based DNA analysis of crime-related specimens. FDLE must purchase approved chemical reagents, supplies, software upgrades and equipment maintenance which is compatible with agency validated equipment and procedures. FDLE crime laboratories will place multiple orders throughout the term of the agreement. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ PUR 7776 (Eff. 01/2016) Page 1 of 2 60A-1.045, F.A.C. In 2008, Life Technologies (now ThermoFisher Scientific) acquired Applied BioSystems®, along with all reagents, consumables, instruments and software previously owned by Applied BioSystems®. The equipment, software and reagents utilized by FDLE were subjected to a rigorous validation and selection process. The validation process at FDLE began with the evaluation of instrumentation, equipment, software and chemistries provided by multiple vendors. The selection was based upon the needs of the customers and the quality of the work product provided by this equipment, software and reagents. Once the standard was selected, a stringent validation process was performed to determine the limitations of the product in order to define the Standard Operating Procedures. These instruments that have been tested and validated require a service contract for periodic maintenance and technical support. All proprietary instruments must be serviced by Life Technologies due to the certification and training of their service engineers, access to instruments, software upgrades and authorized replacement parts. Due to the standardized validation process and proprietary equipment, the chemical reagents, supplies, software upgrades and equipment maintenance is only available through Life Technologies Corporation. Certified Woman-, Veteran- and/or Minority-Owned Business Enterprises are encouraged to participate in the solicitation process.

Protest and Disputes

Any person who is adversely affected by the decision or intended decision made by the Department pursuant to this solicitation shall file with the Department a Notice of Protest in writing within 72 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and state holidays) after the posting of the notice of decision or intended decision. The formal written protest shall be filed within 10 days after the date the Notice of Protest is filed.

With respect to a protest of the terms, conditions and specifications contained in this solicitation, including any provisions governing the methods for ranking bids, awarding contracts, reserving rights of further negotiation, or modifying or amending any contract, the Notice of Protest shall be filed in writing within 72 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and state holidays) after the posting of the solicitation. Also, a summary of the application, payment and any supporting documents submitted by a licensee are uploaded into the OnBase Document Management System. The information submitted by the applicant/licensee is then available in Versa: Regulation and OnBase for department staff to view and process. This system and software is essential in assisting the DBPR in carrying out the General Licensing Provisions as directed in Section 455.213, Florida Statutes. DBPR's license agreement with Tyler for this proprietary software restricts release of the database schema. Access to the database schema would be required in order for competing vendors to offer software that would function with the business rules and configurations of Versa: Regulation and Versa: Online. Short Description: Purchase of Under Bridge Inpection Machine Commodity: 25174800 Specialized vehicle systems and components; 24101500 Industrial trucks Quantity: Two (2) Years Requestor: Maintenance Office, Renee Matthews Requirements: The current truck mounted under bridge inspection machines in the department fleet have been in service for over 10 years and are due for replacement. The budget amount is needed to reduce the backlog of replacement needs experienced by the Department. The funds will provide equipment that will have more reliability and energy efficient. Bridges are required to be inspected every two years at a minimum. Many bridges require the use of a truck mounted under bridge inspection machine in order to provide a comprehensive inspection to ensure that they are safe and structurally sound. Special inspections are also needed to inspect for damage after accidents or natural disasters. The Department of Transportation owns and operates as part of the Department fleet 6 bridge inspection trucks. These trucks were procured in 2010 and 2011 and after 11 years of use, some systems and components deteriorate and the cost of maintaining these items increases. Component failures may cause costly down time, safety issues, and can require additional work for our maintenance personnel that can be avoided. These trucks have been in service for over 11 years and are due for rebuild or replacement. The budget amount is needed to reduce the backlog of replacement needs experienced by the Department. The funds will provide equipment that will have more reliability and more energy efficient. The under- bridge inspection trucks are essential for the Department to maintain safety and mobility of the state Intended Source: Aspen Aerials, Inc. The A-62T under bridge inspection truck allows department employees to perform bridge inspections, maintenance, and repairs of the state bridge network. This includes, but it is not limited to fracture critical, in-depth, and emergency bridge inspections, non-destructive testing on bridge components, deck and pier patching, resealing bridge joints, superstructure repairs, resetting and replacing bridge bearings, and preventative maintenance activities such as drain cleaning, vegetation removal, bearing lubrication, concrete and structural steel coating applications on bridge superstructure and substructure elements. matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) Title: Under Bridge Inspection Machine Purchase Agency number: DOT-SS-22-9117-MC Commodity codes: 25174800 Specialized vehicle systems and components; 24101500 Industrial trucks Posting:

This description of commodities or contractual services intended for purchase from a single source is posted in accordance with section 120.57(3), Florida Statues and will remain posted for a period of 3 business days.

The Florida Department of Transportation intends to enter into a single source contract with 

Aspen Aerials, Inc.

Short Description: Purchase of Under Bridge Inpection Machine Commodity: 25174800 Specialized vehicle systems and components; 24101500 Industrial trucks Requestor: Maintenance Office, Renee Matthews Requirements: The current truck mounted under bridge inspection machines in the department fleet have been in service for over 10 years and are due for replacement. The budget amount is needed to reduce the backlog of replacement needs experienced by the Department. The funds will provide equipment that will have more reliability and energy efficient. Bridges are required to be inspected every two years at a minimum. Many bridges require the use of a truck mounted under bridge inspection machine in order to provide a comprehensive inspection to ensure that they are safe and structurally sound. Special inspections are also needed to inspect for damage after accidents or natural disasters. The Department of Transportation owns and operates as part of the Department fleet 6 bridge inspection trucks. These trucks were procured in 2010 and 2011 and after 11 years of use, some systems and components deteriorate and the cost of maintaining these items increases. Component failures may cause costly down time, safety issues, and can require additional work for our maintenance personnel that can be avoided. These trucks have been in service for over 11 years and are due for rebuild or replacement. The budget amount is needed to reduce the backlog of replacement needs experienced by the Department. The funds will provide equipment that will have more reliability and more energy efficient. The under-bridge inspection trucks are essential for the Department to maintain safety and mobility of the state Intended Source: Aspen Aerials, Inc Price: $4,666,625.00 Justification: The Department of Transportation owns and operates 6 underbridge inspection trucks model A-62 from Aspen Aerials, incorporated of Duluth, Minnesota. Aspen Aerials is the manufacture, designer, and builder of the model A-62T under bridge inspection truck. The A-62T has been in production for more than two years. The A-62T under bridge inspection truck allows department employees to perform bridge inspections, maintenance, and repairs of the state bridge network. This includes, but it is not limited to fracture critical, in-depth, and emergency bridge inspections, non-destructive testing on bridge components, deck and pier patching, resealing bridge joints, superstructure repairs, resetting and replacing bridge bearings, and preventative maintenance activities such as drain cleaning, vegetation removal, bearing lubrication, concrete and structural steel coating applications on bridge superstructure and substructure elements. Aspen Aerials is the only manufacturer that can supply a unit with all the features listed below. They inclu 1. The ability for booms to deploy or rotate off both sides of the vehicle 2. Operate within a 8’-6” lane, move with the unit deployed, without the use of outriggers. 3. Counterweight that remain within the width of the body when the booms are deployed (this also complies with ANSI requirements) 4. Minimum length of boom No. 2 is 24’ long 5. Equipped with a hydraulically telescoping 4th boom which provides 14’ of vertical height 6. Equipped with a 18

To accomplish this, FDLE’s laboratory personnel use the QIASymphony to analyze and sample DNA of crime-related specimens. The hardware necessary to grow the system and expand the amount of work completed within our current infrastructure is proprietary to and manufactured solely by Qiagen. The QIAsymphony system is augmented by the QIAgility liquid handling system. The QIAsymphony and QIAgility systems are the only ones that are validated to work with the QIAGEN EZ1 extraction robot already in place in FDLE’s crime laboratories. FDLE currently has 40 QIAGEN instruments in operation and these QIAGEN instruments require QIAGEN supplies and implements which can only be purchased through QIAGEN, LLC. Short Description: Data collection services of sideway-force coefficient of friction, macrotexture, grade, cross-slope, and horizontal curvature by a Sideway-force Coefficient Routine Investigation Machine (SCRIM), along roadways at the closest interval reporting lengths available. Commodity: Traffic control: 46161500 The sideway-force coefficient of friction, macrotexture, grade, cross-slope, and horizontal curvature data shall be collected by a SCRIM along roadways at the closest interval reporting lengths available. All collected data must be geolocated and Global Positioning System (GPS) linked. The data results shall be provided in Comma Separated Values (CSV) and Geographical Information System (GIS) shape file formats linked to Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT)’s road network. Quantity: 2,000 lane miles Requestor: District 7 Safety Office, William Riha Requirements: The continuous friction measurement data will be utilized to illustrate the role of pavement friction in safety and pavement performance. This will assist in decision- making, monitoring, and managing resources. The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) recently added continuous friction measurement to its list of proven safety countermeasures. It says measuring, monitoring, and maintaining pavement friction can prevent many roadway departure crashes, resulting in fewer serious injuries and fatalities. FHWA goes on to call continuous friction measurement an improvement over traditional spot-based methods of measuring friction and a best practice for targeting “more efficient and effective installations” of friction-enhancing treatments. Intended Source: WDM USA Amount: $299,000.00 Justification: The typical method of measuring friction on roadway networks, in the United States, only takes sample data at extensive defined intervals due to the capabilities of the typical collection machines. These samples are generally not taken on curves or intersections and result in gaps in the collected data, which can potentially result in missed opportunities to proactively identify areas that require enhanced pavement friction to prevent lane departure crashes. Short Description: Data collection services of sideway-force coefficient of friction, macrotexture, grade, cross-slope, and horizontal curvature by a Sideway-force Coefficient Routine Investigation Machine (SCRIM), along roadways at the closest interval reporting lengths available. Commodity: Traffic control: 46161500 The sideway-force coefficient of friction, macrotexture, grade, cross-slope, and horizontal curvature data shall be collected by a SCRIM along roadways at the closest interval reporting lengths available. All collected data must be geolocated and Global Positioning System (GPS) linked. The data results shall be provided in Comma Separated Values (CSV) and Geographical Information System (GIS) shape file formats linked to Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT)’s road network. It says measuring, monitoring, and maintaining pavement friction can prevent many roadway departure crashes, resulting in fewer serious injuries and fatalities. FHWA goes on to call continuous friction measurement an improvement over traditional spot-based methods of measuring friction and a best practice for targeting “more efficient and effective installations” of friction-enhancing treatments. Short Description: This is a gas chromatograph with a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer. Quantity: One GC Triple quad mass spectrometer. Requestor: Raymond Allum , Division of Food Safety Requirements: The Division of Food Safety, Bureau of Laboratories is seeking to purchase an Agilent 7010 EI/MS/MS mass spectrometer for the analysis of samples supporting the Division of Food Safety regulatory Program and the USDA Pesticide Data Program (PDP). Intended Single Source: AGILENT TECHNOLOGIES Amount: ______________________________________________________________________________ Justification: The following specifications are unique to the Agilent 7010 EI/MS/MS instrument and no other manufacturer can meet the specifications: 1. The system and associated data acquisition and control software must be compatible with customer’s existing methods created using Agilent Mass Hunter software, to include acquisition parameters, processing methods, and reports. This platform will be one of three systems generating data for the State and PDP programs. It is critical for employee training and sample workload demands that all systems share similar methods, reports, and acquisition/control software. 2. The mass spectrometer ion source must have a self-cleaning feature. The only other option on the market is manually cleaning the mass spectrometer ion source. Manually cleaning the ion source is unacceptable because it requires instrument downtime preventing the analysis of samples. Only Agilent Technologies can provide the EI/MS/MS that meets the compatibility specifications as provided above. Raymond Allum, to the best of his knowledge, knows no other company that has a self-cleaning source. The Division of Food Safety, Bureau of Laboratories request that this purchase be carried out on a single source basis. A written price quote is attached for the instrument. matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) Title: Dynamic Friction Tester Agency number: DOT-SS-23-9060-DG Commodity codes: 41114200 Land surveying instruments Posting:

This description of commodities or contractual services intended for purchase from a single source is posted in accordance with Section 287.057(5) ©, Florida Statutes and will remain posted for a period of at least 15 business days.

The Department of Transportation intends to enter into a single source contract with Shima American Corporation for Dynamic Friction Tester.

Short Description: Instrument used to measure skid resistance. Commodity: 4111420 - Land surveying equipment. Quantity: One (1) DF Tester (USB Version) & 30 sets (90 pieces) of DFT Rubber Slider. Requestor: Precious Merriweather, State Materials Office. Requirements: DFTester is an instrument to measure skid resistance. The measurement result is shown as a Coefficient of Friction (μ). DFTester has a disk with 3 rubber sliders mounted on the lower surface that spins with its plane parallel to the test surface. Water is introduced in front of the sliders. The disk drops down on the test surface when the rotating speed reaches a target speed. The speed of the driving device gradually decreases due to the friction between rubber sliders and the test surface, and finally stops. This instrument can be operated any place(s) where you can secure the space for the disk to rotate. (Measurement on a slope depends on its angle). Also, you can grasp the relationship between skid resistance and speed as measuring speed can be maintained by rotating the driving disk. This is a portable type instrument, and is easy to carry. Intended Source: Shima American Corporation. Amount: $43,872.95 Justification: The Dynamic Friction Tester (DFT) is a piece of equipment that collects data used for determining the frictional characteristics of laboratory samples, in-place materials, and Department infrastructures to ensure skid resistant surfaces. These tests are required to remain in compliance with the Federal Highway Administration’s National Guidelines given in the 1980 Skid Accident Reduction Program (t-5040.17), and the 2009 AASHTO Guide for Pavement Friction. The Dynamic Friction Tester was developed by and is solely manufactured by Nippo Sangyo in Japan. Shima American Corporation is the exclusive distributor in North America.

Snider Tire, Inc., is the sole U.S. distributor of the WheelRight Tyre Management Technology System and Services. The WheelRight TMS is a drive-through tire monitoring system that allows drivers of passenger vehicles to measure their tire pressure and tread depth without exiting their vehicle while visiting a service plaza on Florida's Turnpike. The WheelRight TMS was opened to the public at the Turkey Lake Service Plaza in November 2021. Snider Tire, Inc., will continue to provide the maintenance of the WheelRight tire pressure and tire tread measurement system equipment, software and license services. Intended Source: Snider Tire, Inc., dba Snider Fleet Solutions Amount: $150,000.00 Justification: According to the U.S. Department of Transportation, National Highway Safety Traffic Administration, there were 664 tire- related motor vehicle traffic fatalities in 2020. Proper tire pressure is the most important part of maintaining tires. The Department has installed an easy-to-use drive-through tire pressure and depth monitoring system at no cost to the driver. This system provides drivers of passenger cars, tire pressure and tread depth measurements in seconds without the drivers having to exit their vehicles. Drivers can print the results of the readings at a kiosk located just feet away or elect to have results sent to a cell phone via text, or by email. • WheelRight Limited holds patents on the drive-through TMS the Department seeks to utilize. • Snider Tire, Inc. is the only authorized distributor of WheelRight's Tyre Management System and Services in the U.S. The TMS product and services are exclusive to WheelRight Tyre Management Technology. Snider Tire, Inc. has the only U.S. partnership agreement to maintain the WheelRight's patented drive-through TMS. In addition to the TMS, the designated service plaza is currently equipped with free air stands. Drivers can test their tire pressure and tire tread depth measurements and inflate their tires in one (1) location at the service plaza. The free services offered to the public can reduce the number of tire-related incidents and save lives on Florida's Turnpike. Approved By: (names & titles, as appropriate to Post on Ven

matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) Title: Dynamic Friction Tester Agency number: DOT-SS-23-9060-DG Commodity codes: 41114200 Land surveying instruments Posting:

This description of commodities or contractual services intended for purchase from a single source is posted in accordance with Section 287.057(5) ©, Florida Statutes and will remain posted for a period of at least 3 business days.

The Department of Transportation intends to enter into a single source contract with Shima American Corporation for Dynamic Friction Tester.

Short Description: Instrument used to measure skid resistance. Commodity: 4111420-Land surveying equipment Requestor: Precious Merriweather, State Materials Office. Requirements: DFTester is an instrument to measure skid resistance. The measurement result is shown as a Coefficient of Friction (μ). DFTester has a disk with 3 rubber sliders mounted on the lower surface that spins with its plane parallel to the test surface. Water is introduced in front of the sliders. The disk drops down on the test surface when the rotating speed reaches a target speed. The speed of the driving device gradually decreases due to the friction between rubber sliders and the test surface, and finally stops. This instrument can be operated any place(s) where you can secure the space for the disk to rotate. (Measurement on a slope depends on its angle). Also, you can grasp the relationship between skid resistance and speed as measuring speed can be maintained by rotating the driving disk. This is a portable type instrument, and is easy to carry. Intended Source: Shima American Corporation Price: $43,872.95 Justification: The Dynamic Friction Tester (DFT) is a piece of equipment that collects data used for determining the frictional characteristics of laboratory samples, in-place materials, and Department infrastructures to ensure skid resistant surfaces. These tests are required to remain in compliance with the Federal Highway Administration’s National Guidelines given in the 1980 Skid Accident Reduction Program (t-5040.17), and the 2009 AASHTO Guide for Pavement Friction. The Dynamic Friction Tester was developed by and is solely manufactured by Nippo Sangyo in Japan. Shima American Corporation is the exclusive distributor in North America. FDLE must purchase approved chemical reagents, supplies, software upgrades and equipment maintenance which is compatible with agency validated equipment and procedures. ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $6,200,000.00 Justification: The FDLE crime laboratories have purchased equipment from Applied BioSystems® since 2006. The validation process at FDLE began with the evaluation of instrumentation, equipment, software and chemistries provided by multiple vendors. All proprietary instruments must be serviced by Life Technologies due to the certification and training of their service engineers, access to instruments, software upgrades and authorized replacement parts. matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Gaming Control Commission (FGCC) Title: Integrity Monitoring System Agency number: None Commodity codes: 81112200 Software maintenance and support Posting:

The Integrity Monitoring System provides a central management system to account for daily wagering activity at all Florida pari-mutuel facilities, associated tax liabilities and tax payments submitted to Florida Gaming Control Commission (FGCC). Additionally, the system provides an independent monitoring system that connects to the pari-mutuel totalizator systems to download wagering data and test for compliance with Chapters 550, 551, and section 849.086, Florida Statutes, and Chapters 75-2 through 75-15, Florida Administrative Code. 

Spectra Systems Corporation is the developer of the Integrity Monitoring System and has proprietary rights to the system. The Integrity Monitoring System is specifically designed to incorporate the unique regulatory requirements and tax structure in Florida. This automated system mitigates the need for labor intensive reconciliations and serves as the central repository for years of daily wagering activity.

Short Description: High Capacity Geosynthetic Direct Shear Machine Commodity: 11111500, 22101900, 41113900 Quantity: One (1) - High Capacity Geosynthetic Direct Shear Machine Requestor: Brandi Bertram Requirements: The State Materials Office currently performs direct shear testing for materials used in the design of Mechanically Stabilized Earthen Walls (MSE Walls). The test is performed in accordance with the AASHTO and FM T-236 test methodology for soil materials. The test method requires the maximum size of the soil particles be such that the test chamber is no less than six times the maximum particle size. For the device the lab currently uses, the maximum size particle of soil able to be tested is 2.24mm. Construction allows for the use of larger particle sizes (up to 2 inches) for soil materials. In many areas of Florida, including South Florida, Limerock materials may have a significant portion (over 50%) over this particle size, requiring the test be performed on materials that do not fully constitute the full scope of material gradation used onsite and provide an ultra-conservative friction angle result. By purchasing this device, the laboratory will be able to test significantly larger particles which would be more representative of materials used in the construction of the MSE Walls. A study performed by FHWA found that testing larger particle sizes increased the friction angles by 5-6 degrees. Implementing this equipment would allow for the use of materials in MSE walls that would have failed testing at smaller particle sizes to pass with larger particle sizes (increasing the availability of backfill materials for construction). There are no available alternatives to this device.

Short Description: Peraton Integration of FDC and FHP data in LInX system Quantity: Six (6) months Requestor: FDLE/Investigation and Forensic Science (IFS) Requirements: Maintenance and support of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement’s (FDLE) Florida Regional LInX system that provides investigative data from records management systems (RMS), jail management systems (JMS), Computer-aided Dispatch (CAD) systems, pawn systems, and registries to law enforcement agencies nationwide. The current LInX system was acquired through a competitive solicitation (ITN) from Northrop Grumman Corporation in 2015 and is an essential element in maintaining law enforcement data sharing. Since the initial implementation, FDLE has acquired additional data and connections for the LInX system, including RMS, JMS, CAD, pawn and an interface with another data sharing system, FINDER. ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $44,000 Justification: The Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS) launched the LInX initiative in 2003 and the program code is owned by the Federal Government. As a result of federal contract N00173-22- D-2005, Peraton, Inc. is the sole provider of maintenance, enhancements, and changes to the LInX system. Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) Title: High Capacity Geosynthetic Direct Shear Machine Agency number: DOT-SS-23-9098-PB PUR 7778 Commodity codes: 11111500 Dirt and soil; 22101900 Building construction machinery and accessories; 41113900 Soil measuring equipment Posting:

Short Description: High Capacity Geosynthetic Direct Shear Machine Commodity: 11111500, 22101900, 41113900 Requestor: Brandi Bertram Requirements: The State Materials Office currently performs direct shear testing for materials used in the design of Mechanically Stabilized Earthen Walls (MSE Walls). The test is performed in accordance with the AASHTO and FM T-236 test methodology for soil materials. The test method requires the maximum size of the soil particles be such that the test chamber is no less than six times the maximum particle size. For the device the lab currently uses, the maximum size particle of soil able to be tested is 2.24mm. Construction allows for the use of larger particle sizes (up to 2 inches) for soil materials. In many areas of Florida, including South Florida, Limerock materials may have a significant portion (over 50%) over this particle size, requiring the test be performed on materials that do not fully constitute the full scope of material gradation used onsite and provide an ultra-conservative friction angle result. By purchasing this device, the laboratory will be able to test significantly larger particles which would be more representative of materials used in the construction of the MSE Walls. A study performed by FHWA found that testing larger particle sizes increased the friction angles by 5-6 degrees. Implementing this equipment would allow for the use of materials in MSE walls that would have failed testing at smaller particle sizes to pass with larger particle sizes (increasing the availability of backfill materials for construction). Requirements: The FDOT Surveying and Mapping personnel provide Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) carrier phase and code range measurements in support of 3- dimensional positioning activities for work programs throughout the State, using the Florida Permanent Reference Network (FPRN). The existing GNSS receivers used to collect this information at the individual sites are reaching end of life. Upgrading these units will allow the FPRN to track additional frequencies broadcast by the GNSS satellites. The existing antennas have been in place, in the field, for several years. End Date and Time:         November 13, 2023 @ 3:00 PM (ET)

Please see the attached PUR 7776 form for additional information.

Short Description: Procurement of a SCIEX Triple Quad 7500 System; an enhanced high-performance triple Quadrupole LC-MS/MS Mass Spectrometer. Quantity: Approximately 12 months Requestor: Division of Environmental Assessment and Restoration (DEAR), Bureau of Labs, Chemistry Program Requirements: Purchase of a SCIEX Triple Quad 7500 System; an enhanced high performance triple quadrupole LC-MS/MS mass spectrometer. The instrument upgrade is expected to aid in achieving lower detection limits, provide improved turn-around times, and facilitate method performance improvements. Quote Subtotal: $541,868.18 Less Additional Discount Total: - $33,527.65 ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $520.182.79 Justification: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Chemistry Program, seeks to augment its analytical Ultra High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (UPLC) capabilities with the acquisition of an efficient liquid chromatograph/triple quadrupole mass spectrometer (LC/MSMS) for organic analysis. The LC/MSMS instrument is needed to handle an ongoing shortfall of UPLC trace-level analytical capacity. To adequately meet the needs of the chemistry laboratory, it is imperative to obtain instrumentation to provide enhanced analytical capabilities. The LC/MSMS specifications, computer software, and data file format for the new instrument must be compatible with our existing equipment to maintain consistency, exchangeability, and integration. The Florida Department of Transportation, Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise, an executive agency of the State of Florida (Department), desires to enter into a single source contract with Q-Free America, Inc. (Q-Free), to procure three (3) years of software maintenance and support services and enhancements for the following Q-Free America, Inc. products: 1) Intrada® Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) and 2) Intrada® Synergy Server (ISS).

Short Description: Q-Free’s Intrada®SynergyServer(ISS) and Intrada® Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Annual Software Maintenance Support Services. Also included in the scope is software enhancements for both products. Quantity: Three (3) Years Requestor: Jim Fisher Director, Tolls Data Center Florida’s Turnpike Boca Tolls Data Center 7941 Glades Road Boca Raton, Florida 34761 ______________________________________________________________________________ Requirements: TheFloridaDepartment ofTransportation,Florida’s TurnpikeEnterprise, anexecutive agency of the State of Florida (Department), desires to enter into a single source contract with Q-Free America, Inc. (Q-Free), to procure three (3) years of software maintenance and support services and enhancements for the following Q-Free America, Inc. products: 1) Intrada® Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) and 2) Intrada® Synergy Server (ISS). Intrada® Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) The Department currently utilizes Q-Free’s Intrada® OCR software for Toll System Replacemnt (TSR) lanes, which comprise approximately 66% of the Florida Turnpike Enterprise’s (FTE) tolling system. The Department has previously procured Q-Free America, Inc. Intrada® OCR – ALPR Software Maintenance Support Service utilizing a single source. The current Single Source contract for the maintenance and support of the Q-Free America, Inc. Intrada® OCR – ALPR software expires on January 31, 2024. The procurement of the software maintenance and support services for this product is necessary in order to maintain support of Q-Free America, Inc. Intrada® OCR – ALPR software which is required to be tuned to read approximately 60% of Florida standard-issue plates at a 0.05% error rate. Intrada® Synergy Server (ISS) The Department currently utilizes Q-Free’s ISS software to process license plate video transactions from all FTE’s tolling lanes for a Amount: Not to exceed $2,122,296 ______________________________________________________________________________ PUR 7776 (Revised 07/2022) Page 2 of 4 Incorporated by Reference: Rule 60A-1.045, F.A.C. Justification: Q-Free is the sole source provider for the Intrada® Optical Character Recognition (OCR) specific proprietary software components needed to maintain the Department’s production TSR lanes (toll lanes equipped with Raytheon/Vertex and Xerox tolling equipment), which comprise approximately 66% of the FTE tolling system. The OCR software is tuned to read approximately 60% of Florida standard-issue plates at a 0.05% error rate. This low error rate allows the Department to bill that group of video toll customers with no manual review and is a critical component intheDepartment’s overall imageprocessingsolution. Q-Free provides a proprietary centralized Intrada® Synergy Server (ISS) video image processing software for automated toll license plate image processing. All intellectual property and title to the software properties remain the property of Q-Free. Q-Free’s ISS software provides 73% automated plate reads for image transactions with no more than 0.05% error rate for Florida standard-issue plates. This low error rate allows the Department to reduce human review. With 1.6 billion transactions annually, accuracy and automation are of the utmost importance to the Department, and periodic retuning is necessary to maintain financial performance. The traffic volumes have been increasing steadily and the images that are processed have increased as well. The current daily image volumes on weekdays are averaging 1.8M. The original Statement of Work (SOW) had a peak load at 2.6M per day

Notice of intended single-source purchase, Department of Health (DOH) Title: QIAGEN instruments Agency number: EXP2538 Commodity codes: 41113000 Chemical evaluation instruments and supplies; 41113600 Electrical measuring and testing equipment and accessories; 41115800 Clinical and diagnostic analyzers and accessories and supplies Posting:

The Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Public Health Laboratories (BPHL) has the need to purchase the QIAGEN QIAgility and QIAcuity Four which will be used to perform testing with automation on wastewater samples for the surveillance of infectious agents. These instruments will support the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Wastewater Surveillance System (NWSS) which tracks the presence of infectious agents in wastewater to identify outbreak trends early, directs prevention efforts to where they are most needed, and provides additional insight into disease spread that complements other public health surveillance data. 

In accordance with Chapter 60A-1.045, Florida Administrative Code, the Florida Department of Health, BPHL, requests authorization to purchase, as a single source, the QIAgility and QIAcuity Four from QIAGEN.

Quantity: 3 instruments (QIAgility HEPA/UV SYS-FUL-1, QIAgility HEPA/UV SYS-FUL-1, QIAcuity Four PLT-FUL-1) Requestor: Division of Disease Control and Health Protection (DCHP), Bureau of Public Health Laboratories (BPHL). Requirements: The Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Public Health Laboratories (BPHL) has the need to purchase the QIAGEN QIAgility and QIAcuity Four which will be used to perform testing with automation on wastewater samples for the surveillance of infectious agents. These instruments will Amount: $201,453.02. Justification: • The QIAcuity is a digital polymerase chain reaction (PCR) instrument that uses a unique nanoplate microfluidic technology to perform fully automated nucleic acid absolute quantification. The NWSS program requires using a quantitative PCR method. The laboratory currently has a QIAcuity instrument for NWSS, but the additional instrument is needed to expand laboratory capacity and provide redundancy when one instrument is inoperable due to maintenance and repair. By having the same instrument, the laboratory will not need to expend additional staff time and alternative instrument supplies to maintain two separate systems. • The QIAgility is a compact benchtop instrument that enables rapid, high-precision PCR setup. It is unique in that almost all tube and plate formats are supported, the single-channel pipet can process up to 96 samples in 17 minutes, and it is a compact instrument with a very small footprint. This instrument is also part of a total workflow that is integrated with the QIAcuity PCR instrument. There is no other instrument available that is compatible in this way with the QIAcuity PCR instrument. QIAGEN is the sole manufacturer and distributor of the QIAgility and QIAcuity Four. NOTICE OF SINGLE SOURCE procurement for the Florida Department of Transportation:

 

The Department of Transportation, State Materials Office, is requesting information from prospective vendors regarding their ability to supply the services described in the attached document.

 

KNOWN VENDOR: AVEC, Inc.

 

Vendor information must be received by 5:00 p.m. (EST) on Friday, February 9, 2024, at either the e-mail or mailing address listed in this posting.

 

If it is determined in writing by the Department, after reviewing any information received from prospective vendors, that the commodities or contractual services are available only from a single source, the Department will post notice of its intended decision to enter into a single source purchase contract on the Vendor Information Portal, in the manner specified in s. 120.57(3), Florida Statutes.

Short Description: AVEC On-Board Sound Intensity System Commodity: 41115500: Sound generating and measuring equipment; 41112800: Transportation related equipment and instruments; 81141803: Acoustics or noise control Quantity: One (1) OBSI System Requestor: Melanie Sowers, State Materials Office Requirements: As homes and commercial businesses are developed closer to high-speed roadways, noise generated from the tire-pavement interaction is considered an important factor in roadway design. The OBSI Systems measure tire pavement noise interaction at highway speeds to assess noise levels on department roadways based on the current AASHTO standard (T 360-16), which enables the evaluation of the noise performance of the pavement designs and materials. This information has been used to support design specifications, determine noise sensitive areas, and reduce the noise impact on the public. New OBSI technology is equipped with integrated Global Positioning System (GPS) and Distance Measuring Instrument (DMI) to provide reliable noise measurement without any locational error. Intended Source: AVEC, Inc. Amount: $39,000.00 Justification: The current OBSI System is outdated and past its useful service life. The System cannot accurately log Global Positioning System (GPS) nor Distance Measuring Instrument (DMI) units. AVEC, Inc. offers a continuous noise measuring system (on board sound intensity, OBSI) designed for surveying roadways and measuring both (1) noise levels and (2) real-time Global Positioning System (GPS) data simultaneously. There are no other known vendors or systems who have integrated GPS into its data collection equipment/process.

THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR BID OR PROPOSAL. THIS IS STATUTORILY MANDATED FIFTEEN BUSINESS DAY ADVERTISEMENT OF AN INTENDED SINGLE SOURCE PROCUREMENT BY FDLE.

Short Description: A portable x-ray machine with the ability to inspect anomalies within enclosed spaces. Quantity: One (1) Unit Requestor: Investigations and Forensic Science / Protective Operations Requirements: Pursuant to Chapter 943, FS and Chapter 11, FAC, the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE), mission is to promote public safety and strengthen domestic security by providing services in partnership with local, state and federal criminal justice agencies to prevent, investigate, and solve crimes while protecting Florida’s citizens by enforcing and supporting prevention of drug activity, responding to emergency situations and preventing any act of terrorism or criminal violence in the State of Florida. FDLE currently utilizes Research Electronics International, LLC (REI) equipment to conduct technical surveillance countermeasures searches using systems and components such as: OSCAR ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $65,000.00 Justification: Viken Detection is the only company with the ability to detect lead and provide Backscatter and Transmission X-ray images using an attached accessory – the DTX arm. Viken is the only manufacturer of the BTX imager with lead detection and DTX arm. Viken does not use any authorized distributors to sell these products. The Nighthawk - BTX includes a 120 or 140 KeV X-ray source designed to deliver high quality Backscatter Images. These X-rays are purely for imaging purposes and are not capable of locating concealed lead compartments in a particular conveyance. Recognizing this as a major vulnerability, Viken detection has added internal Cadmium Telluride detectors which allows the user to be instantly alerted if lead is detected. No other manufacture in the industry has this capability. This is important because of the limited training that officers receive and their relative inexperience looking at X¬ray images. If an officer were to scan a conveyance that contained a lead compartment, they would see a completely black image on their operating screen. This is because X-rays are absorbed by the lead, and they are unable to penetrate this medium. This description of commodities or contractual services intended for purchase from a single source is posted in accordance with Section 287.057(5) ©, Florida Statutes and will remain posted for a period of at least 15 business days.

The Department of Transportation intends to enter into a single source contract with Preferred Materials, Inc., A CRH Company for Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement (RAP) Base Test Track

Short Description: Test Track paving to test the viability of using unstabilized RAP as a base material. Commodity: 30121600 Quantity: Three (3) months. Requestor: Melanie Sowers, State Materials Office. Requirements: The State Materials Office (SMO) has developed a work plan for its accelerated pavement testing (APT) facility in Gainesville to test the viability of using unstabilized reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) as a base material. The RAP base will be tested to new specification criteria not used on Department projects previously. The work plan will include the removal of existing base and asphalt. A new RAP base will be constructed. New asphalt pavement will also be constructed. The new work plan will include a control and test section. The Department will also be comparing the performance of these sections to previous sections placed at its APT facility. Intended Source: Preferred Materials, Inc. A CRH Company Amount: $99,251.57 Justification: There is a need to use Preferred Materials as the contractor on this project to minimize the differences between the asphalt mixtures placed during the last two paving cycles of the APT facility and those placed during this cycle of paving. Asphalt mix designs are the proprietary property of the contractor and cannot be shared with other contractors. Other contractors producing asphalt in the vicinity of the SMO do not use the same materials or mix designs as Preferred Materials, making them the only known vendor in the State of Florida to provide the services.

Short Description: Radiation Level Detection Devices including repairs and parts. Quantity: Three (3) years Requestor: Lieutenant Artez Lester, FCCM, Florida Highway Patrol, Hazardous Materials Team Statewide Coordinator Requirements: These platforms will be used to enhance the capabilities to detect and identify radiological materials being transported illicitly through the state, pursuant to Section 404.20 F.S. This purchase will add detection platforms whose hardware and software will be interchangeable with _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Amount: Year 1: Up to $1,000,000 Year 2: Up to $1,000,000 Year 3: Up to $1,000,000 Total: Up to $3,000,000 Justification: CVE originally purchased its radiation detection platforms from the manufacturer, Radiation Solutions, Inc. CVE performed test scenarios utilizing live radioactive sources across multiple platforms. CVE determined that no other device had all of the functionality needed to accurately detect, identify and display the characteristics of common isotopes at high speeds, which could be identified on Florida highways while concurrently relaying this information in real-time via an integrated cellular connection. This is the only platform that will integrate with the devices used by partner State and Federal Agencies, and no other radiation level detection devices are compatible with this system. The Department’s existing radiation detection devices are interchangeable with this platform. Radiation Solutions, Inc. is the sole provider of these radiation level detection devices and does not offer their products through any third party vendor. Each component of these platforms can be directly plugged into any of CVE’s existing mobile platforms, if one of their components fail, and doing so will not jeopardize the manufacturer’s original warranty. No other vendor can provide the integration functionality; their components lack the ability to connect to RSI platforms. The validation process at FDLE began with the evaluation of instrumentation, equipment, software and chemistries provided by multiple vendors. The selection was based upon the needs of the customers and the quality of the work product provided by this equipment, software and reagents. Once the standard was selected, a stringent validation process was performed to determine the limitations of the product in order to define the Standard Operating Procedures. These instruments that have been tested and validated require a service contract for periodic maintenance and technical support. All proprietary instruments must be serviced by Life Technologies due to the certification and training of their service engineers, access to instruments, software upgrades and authorized replacement parts. Jason Britt, Florida Highway Patrol, Bureau of Criminal Investigations & Intelligence _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Requirements: The Florida Highway Patrol (FHP), Traffic Homicide Investigation Unit, currently utilizes the CDR Systemtools, that allows crash investigators to retrieve critical data from vehicles involved in crashes. matters.title: BLINK Mobile EV Charging Units and Accessories
matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) Title: BLINK Mobile EV Charging Units and Accessories Agency number: DOT-SS-24-9110-SJ (PUR 7776) Commodity codes: 25175000 Electric vehicle charging systems; 25175001 Electric vehicle portable charger; 25175002 Electric vehicle charging station; 25175003 Electric vehicle charging kit Posting:

NOTICE OF SINGLE SOURCE procurement for the Florida Department of Transportation:

 

The Department of Transportation, Traffic Engineering and Operations Office, is requesting information from prospective vendors regarding their ability to supply the services described in the attached document.

 

KNOWN VENDOR: Blink Network, LLC

 

Vendor information must be received by 5:00 p.m. (EST) on Thursday, June 25, 2024, at either the e-mail or mailing address listed in this posting.

 

If it is determined in writing by the Department, after reviewing any information received from prospective vendors, that the commodities or contractual services are available only from a single source, the Department will post notice of its intended decision to enter into a single source purchase contract on the Vendor Information Portal, in the manner specified in s. 120.57(3), Florida Statutes.

Short Description: Blink Mobile Charger and Wall Mount Commodity: 25175000: Electric vehicle charging systems; 25175001: Electric vehicle portable charger; 25175002: Electric vehicle charging station; 25175003: Electric vehicle charging kit Quantity: 32 Charging Units and 32 Mounts Requestor: Derek Vollmer, Traffic Engineering Requirements: The Florida Department of Transportation’s mission is to provide a safe and efficient transportation system. As part of this, the Department contracts service patrol vehicles to assist motorists. The Department wants to pilot portable electric vehicle (EV) chargers to assist EVs out of charge. The portable EV charger consists of a gas powered generator capable of providing 240V AC charging, 32 amps, and 7.7 kW of continuous power. The portable EV generator includes a charger that is compatible with EVs, with a separate adaptor provided by the end user as needed. The charger can be mounted to and plug directly into the generator, or it can be mounted separately. Intended Source: Blink Network LLC Amount: $140,000.00 Justification: The Blink Charging Unit is a level II portable generator solution that is smaller in size. There are two known smaller units, however, Blink is the the only known unit able to charge a fully discharged EV and provide approximately one mile of range every three minutes. The level III solutions investigated by the Department were all too large. Blink is the only known vendor with a solution that fits the Department's size and performance requirements.

matters.title: OTT Hydromet Water Level Monitoring Equipment
matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Northwest Fla Water Management Dist Title: OTT Hydromet Water Level Monitoring Equipment Agency number: 24S-004 Commodity codes: 41114300 Hydrological instruments Posting:

24S-004 PUR 7776

Short Description: The District plans to purchase multiple units of the following types of monitoring equipment: Sutron XLink 500 data logger with North American 4G LTE, SatLink 3 Logger/Transmitter, and OTT/Sutron EcoLog 1000 Logger/Transmitter Quantity: Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Requestor: Steven Costa, Program Manager, Hydrologic Data Services ______________________________________________________________________________ Requirements: Equipment is needed for remote logging of hydrologic data to be telemetered to and accepted by Aquarius software for near real-time updates on field conditions. The XLink 500 logger provides multiple interfaces and protocols (HTTP, TCP/IP, FTP) for communication and three levels of security configuration. The SatLink 3 loggers transmit data using the GOES Satellite Network with an assigned and unique address. It is required that District data loggers can communicate using the LinkComm Software to be compatable with our current network. Both the XLink and SatLink units have sensor interfaces which allow connection to SDI-12, RS-232, and RS-485 devices which can be programmed using LinkComm software run on field laptop computers, tablets or cell phones. The data can be telemetered over the Verizon network with a removable SIM card or downloaded through Bluetooth connection while on site. Intended Single Source: OTT HydroMet Amount: Up to $115,400.00 Justification: XLink 500 units have removable modems that can accept provisioned SIM cards and allows interchangeability between units. The units communicate using LinkComm software which allows continuity in programming with existing deployed equipment. The SatLink 3 units also use the LinkComm software for data download and programming. The EcoLog 1000 is able to accept a uniquely assigned Verizon SIM card which can be transferred between any EcoLog 1000 unit. The XLink, SatLink and EcoLog data loggers manufactured by OTT Hydromet are uniquely able to provide real time data to our network due to their compatibility with our Aquarius software. The Marsh Master, a tracked amphibious vehicle, will allow improved access in areas where other equipment cannot reach. ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $245,640.00 Justification: Justification for Purchase of Marsh Master for Resource Management in District 1 State Parks District 1 manages over 16,500 acres of wetland and submerged habitats which are frequently inaccessible for resource management which includes prescribed fire and invasive plant control. With almost 900 acres of pristine wet prairie and wet flatwoods at Yellow River Marsh Preserve State Park. The Marsh Master, a tracked amphibious vehicle, will allow improved access in areas where other equipment cannot reach. In particular, the Marsh Master is a low ground pressure vehicle that will improve access to tidal/salt marsh and upland/marsh interfaces with minimum damage to natural resources. The onboard fire suppression package and mower attachment will allow for the establishment of fire containment lines for prescribed burning, wildfire suppression, and support prescribed fire operations in the difficult to manage wet prairie community. Having the ability to limit the amount of wet prairie burned during a prescribed or wildfire has important implications for preserving habitat for rare birds such as the Bachman’s sparrow and rare plants including 6 varieties of imperiled or protected varieties of carnivorous plants, where excluding prescribed fire would be detrimental to local populations. An internet search was conducted to see if there were comparable amphibious vehicles to the Marsh Master. The other brands discovered did not have the implement flexibility of the Marsh Master require

matters.text:
Notice of intended single-source purchase, Department of Health (DOH) Title: Radcal Agency number: EXP2589 Commodity codes: 73152108 Electrical equipment maintenance and repair service Posting:

Per Section 404.22, FS, the Department is obligated to inspect radiation producing machines for operational safety. For those devices used for human medical purposes (medical x-ray systems), the Department checks for both operator and patient safety.  As part of evaluating patient safety, the Department must use equipment that accurately assesses that radiation machine output. To perform this task, the Department currently owns Radcal AGMS-D+ sensors, Radcal 10X6-180 ion chambers and Radcal Accu-Gold+ Touch base units.  To ensure these devices meet acceptable standards for accuracy and they must be recalibrated annually and maintained to operational status so that their measurements may be used to enforce regulatory standards for machine safety. .

In accordance with Chapter 60A-1.045, Florida Administrative Code, the Department’s Bureau of Radiation Control requests authorization to purchase, as a single source, calibration and maintenance services, from Radcal Corporation.

Quantity: 1 Year Requestor: DOH, Division of Emergency Preparedness and Community Support, Bureau of Radiation Control Requirements: Per Section 404.22, FS, the Department is obligated to inspect radiation producing machines for operational safety. For those devices used for human medical purposes (medical x-ray systems), the Department checks for both operator and patient safety. As part of evaluating patient safety, the Department must use equipment that accurately assesses that radiation machine output. To perform this task, the Department currently owns Radcal AGMS-D+ sensors, Radcal 10X6-180 ion chambers and Radcal Accu-Gold+ Touch base units. To ensure these devices meet acceptable standards for accuracy and they must be recalibrated annually and maintained to operational status so that their measurements may be used to enforce regulatory standards for machine safety. . Amount: $47,335.00 Justification: • The Department currently utilizes and owns Radcal equipment to conduct the statutorily required testing and evaluation of radiation output. • Radcal Corporation is the only vendor that can provide the required calibration and maintenance of the equipment. . NOTICE OF SINGLE SOURCE procurement for the Florida Department of Transportation:

 

The Department of Transportation, Maintenance Office (Motor Carrier Size and Weight), is requesting information from prospective vendors regarding their ability to supply the services described in the attached document.

If it is determined in writing by the Department, after reviewing any information received from prospective vendors, that the commodities or contractual services are available only from a single source, the Department will post notice of its intended decision to enter into a single source purchase contract on the Vendor Information Portal, in the manner specified in s. 120.57(3), Florida Statutes.

Short Description: Replacement of the Northbound and Southbound Scales at the Punta Gorda Weigh Stations Commodity: 78121602: Weighing services; 73152109: Industrial weight scale maintenance and rental service; 41111500: Weight measuring instruments; 25191800: Vehicle testing and measuring equipment; 73171504: Measuring or testing instruments manufacture services Quantity: One (1) Year Requestor: Jon Heller, MCSAW Requirements: To enhance safety, improve mobility, and decrease the average commercial vehicle wait time at the Punta Gorda scale facility, FDOT is replacing the current Scale 2 on both northbound and southbound facilities. During the building replacement in 2018, the footprint of the new building encroached on the existing scales. With this encroachment, Scale 2 must be shifted 4 feet to allow for over dimensional trucks to safely pass the facility. This shift in location requires a new scale pit to be constructed, allowing the Department the opportunity to increase the scale length to 86 feet. This additional length will eliminate the need to accumulate weights for longer trucks, decreasing the average wait time on the scales. The new scale system must remain compatible with the existing 7541 scales throughout the state which further reduces maintenance costs by ensuring FDOT has the spare parts necessary to repair the scales. Intended Source: Mettler Toledo, LLC Amount: $767,706.00 Justification: The existing computer systems for the scales were developed by Mettler Toledo and are compatible with the existing 7541 scales throughout the state. Mettler Toledo’s proprietary electronic scales are vital to the Weigh-In-Motion (WIM) system. The Direct Care Careers Center (DCC) platform’s goal is to better support individuals self-directing their Medicaid home and community-based services and supports through consumer directed services (CDS). DCC enables individuals within the CDS program to post their specific support and service needs via the job posting functionality which then matches their service and support needs (via the job posting template) to a direct service worker (DSW) pool of candidates (or registry) who have the required skills, certifications, and credentials to support the individual directing their own service. The DCC system then enables the individual directing their own services to interact with potential candidates (i.e., DSWs) for their job posting within the system to confirm interest, availability, and start the employer recruitment process.

Notice of intended single-source purchase, Department of Health (DOH) Title: Agilent Technologies Agency number: EXP2609 Commodity codes: 41151600 Clinical laboratory instruments Posting:

The DOH, BPHL has the need to purchase two Agilent 1290 Infinity II High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) Systems from Agilent Technologies, Inc.  The Public Health Emergency Preparedness Grant Cooperative Agreement (PHEP) guidelines state that CDC Laboratory Response Network -Chemical (LRN-C) members must purchase instruments the meet the exact specifications for performing LRN-C chemical terrorism methods. Short Description: Ammunition Quantity: 3 years from contract execution Requestor: Division of Criminal Investigations ______________________________________________________________________________ Requirements: The Division intends to purchase Speer Bonded Duty and SinterFire ammunition for law enforcement officers' Department-issued firearms. Pursuant to sections 626.989(7), 943.13(11), and 943.135, Florida Statutes, and Rule 11B-27.00212(13)(a)1., (14), Florida Administrative Code, the Division’s officers are considered state law enforcement officers. They are required to complete scenario-based firearms training and qualify biannually with their Department-issued weapons. This ammunition is necessary for law enforcement officers to effectively fulfill their statutory responsibilities in safeguarding Florida’s citizens. The purchase includes both duty and training ammunition, with the Division specifically seeking duty rounds designed for Department -issued weapons, ensuring high weight retention and deep penetration upon firing. Intended Single Source: Florida Bullet Incorporated Amount: $300,000.00 Justification: Independent ballistics testing was conducted over a three-year period to determine performance of ammunitions when fired through bare gelatin, heavy clothing, wallboard, plywood, steel and auto glass. Additionally, The Division participated in demonstrations alongside five other local law enforcement agencies in Tallahassee. The ballistics data indicated that Speer Bonded Duty ammunition demonstrated the highest effectiveness in supporting the Division’s officers in both training and field operations to fulfill their statutory responsibilities. When fired through heavy clothing, Speer Bonded Duty ammunition achieves optimal expansion without over-penetration, ensuring the protection of life, as officers perform their duties. Speer’s Bonded Duty, G-2, line ammunition is manufactured specifically for law enforcement agencies. SinterFire Frangible projectiles are designed to minimize the environmental hazards associated with the use of lead projectiles. Multiple firearms training ranges throughout the state have added requirements to limit the use of lead projectiles during training. The SinterFire projectile is designed to break apart into small pieces upon impact. Additionally, SinterFire projectiles have a reduced risk of ricochet and splash back which offers greater safety for officers in the training environment. The Department has concluded that Speer ammunition is the best available option for duty ammunition while SinterFire is the preferred option for training ammunitio

Short Description: 4111902-Electronic counters. Automated vehicle and pedestrian counters for use at Wildlife Management Area entrances, trailheads, and other locations. Quantity: 49 PRO Evo Counters & 5 Spare Pyro Evo Counters, 1 year Software Subscription and shipping Requestor: HSC Requirements: Electronic traffic counters provide valuable data on public use and visitation at Wildlife Management Area’s statewide. Currently, there are 200 traffic counters collecting data on area visitation at designated entrances and public use areas daily. EcoCounters utilize Bluetooth and remote wireless data transfer (versus RS232 serial cable requirements of the current solution). EcoCounters also do not have to be removed from the field installation for data transfer. EcoCounters are weather-resistant and do not require additional environental housings and are designed for installation outdoors in remote areas and EcoCounter makes specific installation solutions for their counters versus the myriad homegrown solutions used for current counters. ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $362,570.00 Justification: This vendor exclusively produces vehicle and pedestrian counters and services meeting the required specifications needed for the collection of visitation data. Visitation data provides a tempral and spatial account of Wildlife Management Area visitation and has also been instrumental in other management and reporting such as visitation economic impacts and law enforcement investigations. FWC staff has done extensive research on counter options and EcoCounter is the only solution meeting all required specifications. FWC intends to deploy a combination of infrared pedestrian counters and inductive loop vehicle counters WMA system-wide, replacing the aging and sometimes unreliable or less robust counters currently used. Often, environmental conditions and severe weather events cause irreparable damage to the traffic counters, requiring that they be replaced and collection of data can be time-consuming and inefficient, as the current solution requires the counter to be uninstalled, docked at the office for data download, and then reinitialized and redeployed in the field. EcoCounters utilize Bluetooth and remote wireless data transfer (versus RS232 serial cable requirements of the current solution) which reduces the workload of field staff in collecting the data and reduces the workload and potential error sources for office staff in compiling and processing the acquired data. The intent is to provide real-time water level information that will allow local agencies and the Department to respond accordingly to roadway water level conditions. Intended Source: Hohonu (Kevin Mukai), 2800 Woodlawn Drive. Suite 138. Honolulu, HI. 96822. Amount: $$300,000 Justification: This specialized equipment was evaluated and selected by the Plannning and Environmental Management Office (PLEMO) study for a specific deployment in St. Johns County. This product was chosen due to specific criteria as determined in this study based on the detection needs and operational capabilities of the County for roadways known to flood. St. Johns County had flooding concerns around the waterfront area and determined this product was the best choice due to installation capabilities attached to existing infrastructure. This vendor is the sole provider of the Hohonu Water Level Sensor. The objective is to determine unsafe water levels on the roadway system in order to gather historical data as well as to redirect traffic when flooding events occur.

FDLE must purchase approved chemical reagents, supplies, software upgrades and equipment maintenance which is compatible with agency validated equipment and procedures. ______________________________________________________________________________ Amount: $7,000,000.00 Justification: The FDLE crime laboratories have purchased equipment from Applied BioSystems® since 2006. In 2008, Life Technologies (now ThermoFisher Scientific) acquired Applied BioSystems®, along with all reagents, consumables, instruments and software previously owned by Applied BioSystems®. The equipment, software and reagents utilized by FDLE were subjected to a rigorous validation and selection process. The validation process at FDLE began with the evaluation of instrumentation, equipment, software and chemistries provided by multiple vendors. The selection was based upon the needs of the customers and the quality of the work product provided by this equipment, software and reagents. Once the standard was selected, a stringent validation process was performed to determine the limitations of the product in order to define the Standard Operating Procedures. These instruments that have been tested and validated require a service contract for periodic maintenance and technical support. All proprietary instruments must be serviced by Life Technologies due to the certification and training of their service engineers, access to instruments, software upgrades and authorized replacement parts.
